cover.title: Your First Home, Step by Step.
cover.label: FIRST HOME

lines.text: The typical first-time home buyer is now 40 years old.
lines.say: The typical first-time home buyer is now forty years old.

lines.text: That's a record, and first-time buyers made up just 21% of purchases, also a record low.
lines.say: That's a record. And first-time buyers made up just twenty-one percent of purchases, also a record low.

lines.text: Here's that first-time buyer share over five years of NAR surveys.
lines.say: Here's that first-time buyer share, over five years of N A R surveys.

scene.title: First-time buyers' share of home purchases (NAR, %)

lines.text: It fell from 34% in 2021 to 21% in 2025, the lowest NAR has ever recorded.
lines.say: It fell from thirty-four percent in twenty twenty-one, to twenty-one percent in twenty twenty-five. The lowest N A R has ever recorded.

scene.title: First-time buyers' share of home purchases (NAR, %)

lines.text: Prices are part of it. The median existing home sold for $429,100 in August 2026.
lines.say: Prices are part of it. The median existing home sold for about four hundred twenty-nine thousand dollars in August twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: And in late September 2026, the average 30-year mortgage rate topped 7% for the first time since January 2025.
lines.say: And in late September twenty twenty-six, the average thirty-year mortgage rate topped seven percent, for the first time since January twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: But people still buy homes every day. The process is long, but it's the same seven steps for almost everyone.
lines.say: But people still buy homes every day. The process is long, but it's the same seven steps for almost everyone.

lines.text: We'll walk through each one, with the real rules, real math, and the mistakes to avoid.
lines.say: We'll walk through each one, with the real rules, the real math, and the mistakes to avoid.

lines.text: None of it is secret. Most of the rules are public, and the math fits on a napkin.
lines.say: None of it is secret. Most of the rules are public, and the math fits on a napkin.

lines.text: Chapter one: the money check.
lines.say: Chapter one. The money check.

lines.text: Step one is knowing three numbers: your credit score, your savings, and your monthly debts.
lines.say: Step one is knowing three numbers. Your credit score, your savings, and your monthly debts.

lines.text: Start with your credit reports. You can get them free every week at AnnualCreditReport.com.
lines.say: Start with your credit reports. You can get them free, every week, at annual credit report dot com.

lines.text: Look for errors, like accounts that aren't yours or late payments that weren't late, and dispute them early.
lines.say: Look for errors, like accounts that aren't yours, or late payments that weren't late, and dispute them early. Fixes can take weeks.

lines.text: Your credit score shapes which loans you qualify for and the rate you're offered.
lines.say: Your credit score shapes which loans you qualify for, and the rate you're offered.

lines.text: For example, an FHA loan allows 3.5% down with a score of 580 or higher.
lines.say: For example, an F H A loan allows three and a half percent down, with a credit score of five eighty or higher.

lines.text: Scores from 500 to 579 generally need 10% down for FHA.
lines.say: Scores from five hundred to five seventy-nine generally need ten percent down for F H A.

scene.title: FHA down payment by credit score

lines.text: Lenders also compare your monthly debts to your income. That's your debt-to-income ratio.
lines.say: Lenders also compare your monthly debts to your income. That's called your debt-to-income ratio.

lines.text: Car loans, student loans and card minimums all count. Paying some down before you apply can help.
lines.say: Car loans, student loans and credit card minimums all count. Paying some down before you apply can help your ratio.

lines.text: A common rule of thumb: keep housing costs under about 28% of your gross monthly income.
lines.say: A common rule of thumb is to keep housing costs under about twenty-eight percent of your gross monthly income.

lines.text: On an $80,000 salary, that's about $1,867 a month. Keep that number in mind for chapter three.
lines.say: On an eighty thousand dollar salary, that's about eighteen sixty-seven a month. Keep that number in mind for chapter three.

lines.text: Start gathering documents now: pay stubs, W-2s, tax returns and bank statements. Lenders will ask for all of them.
lines.say: Start gathering documents now. Pay stubs, W-twos, tax returns and bank statements. Lenders will ask for all of them.

lines.text: Chapter two: the down payment and the hidden costs.
lines.say: Chapter two. The down payment, and the hidden costs.

lines.text: Myth: you need 20% down. You don't. Many loans allow much less.
lines.say: Here's a myth: you need twenty percent down. You don't. Many loans allow much less.

lines.text: Some conventional loans allow 3% down, FHA 3.5%, and VA and USDA loans can allow zero for eligible buyers.
lines.say: Some conventional loans allow three percent down, F H A three and a half, and V A and U S D A loans can allow zero, for eligible buyers.

lines.text: On a $429,100 home, here's what each minimum means in cash.
lines.say: On a four hundred twenty-nine thousand dollar home, here's what each of those means in cash.

lines.text: That's a $73,000 gap between 3% and 20% down. A smaller down payment gets you in sooner, but borrows more.
lines.say: That's about a seventy-three thousand dollar gap between three and twenty percent down. A smaller down payment gets you in sooner, but you borrow more.

lines.text: In NAR's 2025 survey, first-time buyers put down a median of 10%.
lines.say: In N A R's twenty twenty-five survey, first-time buyers put down a median of ten percent.

lines.text: Most of it came from personal savings. About a fifth got gifts or loans from family or friends.
lines.say: Most of it came from personal savings. About a fifth got gifts or loans from family or friends.

lines.text: If family helps, lenders usually want a signed gift letter saying it's a gift, not a loan.
lines.say: If family helps, lenders usually want a signed gift letter, saying the money is a gift and not a loan.

lines.text: Put down less than 20% on a conventional loan, and you'll usually pay private mortgage insurance, or PMI.
lines.say: Put down less than twenty percent on a conventional loan, and you'll usually pay private mortgage insurance, or P M I.

lines.text: Federal law lets you ask to cancel PMI at 80% loan-to-value, and it ends automatically at 78%.
lines.say: Federal law lets you ask to cancel P M I at eighty percent loan-to-value, and it ends automatically at seventy-eight.

scene.title: PMI on conventional loans (Homeowners Protection Act)

lines.text: FHA loans have their own mortgage insurance: 1.75% upfront, plus an annual premium that's 0.55% for most borrowers.
lines.say: F H A loans have their own mortgage insurance. One point seven five percent upfront, plus an annual premium that's zero point five five percent for most borrowers.

lines.text: Then there are closing costs: fees for the loan, title, appraisal and more. They often run 2% to 5% of the price.
lines.say: Then there are closing costs. Fees for the loan, the title, the appraisal and more. They often run two to five percent of the price.

lines.text: On a $429,100 home, that's roughly $8,600 to $21,500, on top of the down payment.
lines.say: On a four hundred twenty-nine thousand dollar home, that's roughly eighty-six hundred to twenty-one and a half thousand, on top of the down payment.

lines.text: Mistake number one: draining every dollar for the down payment and leaving nothing for repairs or emergencies.
lines.say: Mistake number one: draining every dollar for the down payment, and leaving nothing for repairs or emergencies.

lines.text: Many people aim to keep a few months of expenses in savings after closing, because homes break.
lines.say: Many people aim to keep a few months of expenses in savings after closing, because homes break, and the landlord is now you.

lines.text: Also check your state's housing finance agency. Many offer down payment help for first-time buyers.
lines.say: Also check your state's housing finance agency. Many offer down payment help for first-time buyers.

lines.text: Chapter three: the payment math.
lines.say: Chapter three. The payment math.

lines.text: Let's run a real example: the August 2026 median price, $429,100, with 10% down.
lines.say: Let's run a real example. The August twenty twenty-six median price, four twenty-nine one hundred, with ten percent down.

lines.text: At 7.03% for 30 years, principal and interest come to about $2,577 a month.
lines.say: At seven point oh three percent for thirty years, principal and interest come to about twenty-five seventy-seven a month.

lines.text: Here's a surprise. In the first month, about $2,262 of that payment is interest. Only about $315 pays down the loan.
lines.say: Here's a surprise. In the first month, about twenty-two sixty-two of that payment is interest. Only about three fifteen pays down the loan.

lines.text: That's how amortization works: early payments are mostly interest, later ones mostly principal.
lines.say: That's how amortization works. Early payments are mostly interest, and later ones are mostly principal.

lines.text: That's before property taxes, homeowners insurance and any PMI, which can add hundreds more.
lines.say: And that's before property taxes, homeowners insurance, and any P M I, which can add hundreds more.

lines.text: Remember the 28% rule? $2,577 alone is more than the $1,867 an $80,000 salary would allow.
lines.say: Remember the twenty-eight percent rule? Twenty-five seventy-seven alone is more than the eighteen sixty-seven that an eighty thousand dollar salary would allow.

scene.title: Rule of thumb vs this home

lines.text: By that rule, you'd need roughly $110,000 of income just to cover principal and interest on the median home.
lines.say: By that rule, you'd need roughly a hundred ten thousand dollars of income, just to cover principal and interest on the median home.

lines.text: Over 30 years, those payments total about $927,800. About $541,600 of that is interest.
lines.say: Over thirty years, those payments total about nine hundred twenty-eight thousand dollars. About five hundred forty-two thousand of that is interest.

lines.text: A 15-year loan cuts that sharply. At the same 7.03%, total interest would be about $240,000, but the payment jumps to about $3,478.
lines.say: A fifteen-year loan cuts that sharply. At the same rate, total interest would be about two hundred forty thousand dollars. But the payment jumps to about thirty-four seventy-eight.

lines.text: In real life, 15-year rates are usually a bit lower than 30-year rates, which tilts the math further.
lines.say: In real life, fifteen-year rates are usually a bit lower than thirty-year rates, which tilts the math even further.

lines.text: The rate matters a lot. At 6%, the same loan's payment would be about $2,315, about $262 less a month.
lines.say: The rate matters a lot. At six percent, the same loan's payment would be about twenty-three fifteen. That's about two hundred sixty-two dollars less, every month.

lines.text: That's why shopping lenders matters. Rates and fees can differ from one lender to the next.
lines.say: That's why shopping lenders matters. Rates and fees can differ from one lender to the next.

lines.text: Ask several lenders for a Loan Estimate. The forms are standardized, so they're easy to compare line by line.
lines.say: Ask several lenders for a Loan Estimate. The forms are standardized, so they're easy to compare line by line.

lines.text: Points are prepaid interest. One point costs 1% of the loan and buys a lower rate.
lines.say: Points are prepaid interest. One point costs one percent of the loan, and buys you a lower rate.

lines.text: Once you're under contract, you can lock your rate, so it can't rise before closing for a set period.
lines.say: Once you're under contract, you can lock your rate, so it can't rise before closing for a set period.

lines.text: Also know the conforming loan limit: $832,750 in most of the US for 2026. Bigger loans are jumbo loans with different rules.
lines.say: Also know the conforming loan limit: eight hundred thirty-two thousand seven hundred fifty dollars in most of the US for twenty twenty-six. Bigger loans are jumbo loans, with different rules.

scene.label: 2026 conforming loan limit (most areas)
scene.sub: one-unit homes (FHFA); higher in pricey areas

lines.text: Chapter four: preapproval and shopping.
lines.say: Chapter four. Preapproval and shopping.

lines.text: Step two: get preapproved. A lender checks your credit, income and assets, and says how much it may lend.
lines.say: Step two: get preapproved. A lender checks your credit, income and assets, and tells you how much it may lend.

lines.text: Don't confuse it with prequalification, which is a quick estimate. Preapproval checks your documents.
lines.say: Don't confuse it with prequalification, which is just a quick estimate. Preapproval actually checks your documents.

lines.text: Sellers take preapproved buyers more seriously. It also tells you your real budget.
lines.say: Sellers take preapproved buyers more seriously. And it tells you your real budget.

lines.text: Preapproval letters usually expire after a few months, so time it close to when you'll really shop.
lines.say: Preapproval letters usually expire after a few months, so time it close to when you'll really shop.

lines.text: Mistake number two: assuming the amount you're approved for is the amount you should spend.
lines.say: Mistake number two: assuming the amount you're approved for is the amount you should spend.

lines.text: The lender's max doesn't know about your daycare bill or your savings goals. You do.
lines.say: The lender's maximum doesn't know about your daycare bill, or your savings goals. You do.

lines.text: Step three: shop for the home, often with a buyer's agent. Agent pay is negotiable, and it's spelled out in a written agreement.
lines.say: Step three: shop for the home, often with a buyer's agent. Agent pay is negotiable, and since twenty twenty-four, it's spelled out in a written agreement before touring.

lines.text: Look past the photos: commute, school district, property taxes, HOA fees and flood zone all affect your real cost.
lines.say: Look past the photos. The commute, the school district, property taxes, H O A fees and flood zone all affect your real cost.

lines.text: Chapter five: offer to closing.
lines.say: Chapter five. From offer to closing.

lines.text: Step four: make an offer. It includes the price, the earnest money deposit, and contingencies.
lines.say: Step four: make an offer. It includes the price, the earnest money deposit, and contingencies.

lines.text: From an accepted offer to closing often takes about a month, sometimes longer.
lines.say: From an accepted offer to closing often takes about a month, and sometimes longer.

lines.text: Earnest money shows you're serious. It goes toward your costs at closing, but you can lose it if you back out without a contingency.
lines.say: Earnest money shows you're serious. It goes toward your costs at closing, but you can lose it if you back out without a contingency.

lines.text: Contingencies are your exits: for example, if the inspection, appraisal or financing falls through.
lines.say: Contingencies are your exits. For example, if the inspection, the appraisal, or the financing falls through.

lines.text: Step five: the inspection. A pro checks the roof, wiring, plumbing and more.
lines.say: Step five: the inspection. A professional checks the roof, the wiring, the plumbing and more.

scene.name: HOME INSPECTION
scene.label: roof, wiring, pipes
scene.caption: Find problems before you own them

lines.text: Mistake number three: skipping the inspection to win a bidding war. Any problems you find later are yours.
lines.say: Mistake number three: skipping the inspection to win a bidding war. Any problems you find later are yours.

lines.text: The lender also orders an appraisal, to confirm the home is worth what you're paying.
lines.say: The lender also orders an appraisal, to confirm the home is worth what you're paying.

lines.text: If the appraisal comes in low, the lender lends less. You may need more cash, a lower price, or the appraisal contingency to exit.
lines.say: If the appraisal comes in low, the lender lends less. You may need more cash, a lower price, or the appraisal contingency to walk away.

lines.text: You'll also buy title insurance, which protects against old ownership claims, and usually set up an escrow account for taxes and insurance.
lines.say: You'll also buy title insurance, which protects against old ownership claims, and usually set up an escrow account for taxes and insurance.

lines.text: Step six: the paperwork. Within 3 business days of applying, the lender must send a Loan Estimate.
lines.say: Step six: the paperwork. Within three business days of applying, the lender must send you a Loan Estimate.

lines.text: And you must get the Closing Disclosure at least 3 business days before closing.
lines.say: And you must get the Closing Disclosure at least three business days before closing.

lines.text: Compare the two. If fees jumped, ask why before you sign.
lines.say: Compare the two forms. If the fees jumped, ask why before you sign.

lines.text: Step seven: closing. You sign, pay the down payment and closing costs, and get the keys.
lines.say: Step seven: closing. You sign, pay the down payment and closing costs, and get the keys.

lines.text: Right before closing, do a final walk-through to make sure the home is in the condition you agreed to.
lines.say: Right before closing, do a final walk-through, to make sure the home is in the condition you agreed to.

lines.text: And bring the funds the way your closing agent says, usually a wire or cashier's check, and call to confirm wire details by phone.
lines.say: And bring the funds the way your closing agent says, usually a wire or a cashier's check. And confirm any wire instructions by phone, because scammers fake those emails.

lines.text: Mistake number four: opening new credit or changing jobs before closing. Lenders can recheck right before the end.
lines.say: Mistake number four: opening new credit, or changing jobs, before closing. Lenders can recheck right before the end.

lines.text: Chapter six: the one-screen checklist.
lines.say: Chapter six. The one-screen checklist.

lines.text: One: check your credit, savings and debts.
lines.say: One: check your credit, savings and debts.

lines.text: Two: save for the down payment and closing costs, plus a cushion.
lines.say: Two: save for the down payment and closing costs, plus a cushion.

lines.text: Three: get preapproved, and compare lenders.
lines.say: Three: get preapproved, and compare lenders.

lines.text: Four: shop, and make an offer with contingencies.
lines.say: Four: shop, and make an offer with contingencies.

lines.text: Five through seven: inspection and appraisal, the paperwork, and closing.
lines.say: Five through seven: the inspection and appraisal, the paperwork, and closing.

lines.text: And the four mistakes: no cushion, max budget, skipped inspection, new credit before closing.
lines.say: And the four mistakes: no cash cushion, spending the max, skipping the inspection, and new credit before closing.

lines.text: And the math to remember: median home, 10% down, 7.03%, about $2,577 a month before taxes and insurance.
lines.say: And the math to remember. The median home, ten percent down, at seven point oh three percent: about twenty-five seventy-seven a month, before taxes and insurance.

lines.text: Buying a home is a long checklist, not a mystery. Now you have it.
lines.say: Buying a home is a long checklist, not a mystery. And now you have it.

lines.text: If this helped, subscribe for more of The Guide.
lines.say: If this helped, subscribe for more of The Guide.

post.yt_desc:
The typical first-time home buyer is now 40 years old and first-time buyers were a record-low 21% of purchases (NAR, 2025). We walk through all seven steps of buying a first home: the money check, down payments and closing costs, the payment math on the August 2026 median price, preapproval and shopping, offer to closing, and a one-screen checklist with the four most common mistakes.

CHAPTERS

Sources:
- NAR 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers (Nov 2025)
- NAR Existing-Home Sales, August 2026
- Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (Sept 24, 2026)
- HUD/FHA loan requirements; FHFA 2026 conforming loan limits
- CFPB Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure rules
- Homeowners Protection Act (PMI cancellation)

News and education, not financial advice.
